guidance: Explain what it sells, who pays, and why in five sentences or fewer.
primary_value: Lam makes extremely precise machines that chipmakers use to add, remove and clean microscopic layers on silicon wafers. As chips gain more layers and harder structures, customers need more of Lam's tools and service. The machines are valuable and difficult to replace, but chip factories spend in cycles and governments can restrict where the tools are sold.

guidance: Why could customers keep choosing it?
primary_value: A best-in-class semiconductor-equipment compounder with record FY2026 revenue, 35.3% GAAP operating margin, a growing service base, more than 40,000 conductor-etch chambers and strong exposure to AI-driven memory, foundry and advanced packaging.

guidance: What is the least flattering accurate description?
primary_value: A cyclical capital-equipment supplier priced for sustained AI/WFE growth, exposed to China and export controls, customer concentration, product-transition risk, single-source components and a free-cash-flow yield near 1.3% at the verified pre-earnings quote.

guidance: This is actually a [business type] powered by [engine], not merely a [narrative] company.
primary_value: Lam earns high-value system revenue from deposition, etch and clean tools, then monetizes the installed base through spares, service, upgrades and Equipment Intelligence. FY2026 revenue was $23.23 billion; the June quarter included $4.25 billion of systems and $2.47 billion of customer-support revenue.

guidance: Which product, segment, or transaction produces the profit?
primary_value: The core profit pool is process-critical etch and deposition equipment, reinforced by a recurring installed-base service stream. Greater device complexity raises process steps and Lam content per wafer even when unit growth is slower.

guidance: What matters most that management cannot control?
primary_value: Customer wafer-fab-equipment budgets are the largest outside dependency. AI infrastructure, memory utilization and foundry technology transitions support demand, while export controls, geopolitics and customer capex pauses can override company execution.

guidance: State the growth, margin, share, and execution assumptions required by the current price.
primary_value: Using the latest independently verified pre-earnings quote of $291.61 and June 28 shares outstanding, market value is about $364.9 billion and enterprise value about $363.0 billion. That equals 50.6x FY2026 GAAP EPS and 74.6x FY2026 free cash flow, implying sustained WFE outperformance, strong margins and successful next-generation products. Refresh the quote before any trade.

guidance: Which businesses are truly comparable, and where are they not?
primary_value: Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron are the closest broad wafer-fab-equipment peers; KLA is the key process-control comparator. ASML and ASM International are useful partial comparisons. Lam is particularly concentrated in etch, deposition, memory and installed-base productivity.

guidance: What remains if the most exciting future product receives zero value?
primary_value: Even assigning zero value to Dextro robotics, Semiverse Solutions or dry-photoresist optionality, Lam's installed etch/deposition/clean franchise and customer-support business are excellent. The problem is price: today's multiple already requires substantial earnings growth from the proven core.

guidance: What useful asset, process, relationship, skill, resource, or system has the company built?
primary_value: Lam's key demonstrated capability is co-optimizing hardware, process recipes, materials, software and control for the most difficult deposition and etch steps, then learning from a very large installed base.

guidance: Is it a claim, capability, trajectory, proven moat, eroding moat, or no moat? Why?
primary_value: Proven but cyclical moat. Qualification costs, process integration, R&D scale, customer co-development, proprietary recipes and the installed base are durable advantages. They do not eliminate WFE cycles, export restrictions or technology-transition risk.

guidance: What evidence most strongly argues against the moat conclusion?
primary_value: The strongest counterevidence is that excellent FY2026 execution coincides with an extreme valuation. China represented 26% of the June quarter and 37% of revenue in the nine months through March, while receivables, DSO and inventory rose into year-end.

guidance: What creates revenue, profit, and cash now?
primary_value: Current value is generated by deposition, etch and clean systems plus the Customer Support Business Group. CSBG was $2.47 billion, or 36.8% of June-quarter revenue, providing a meaningful installed-base layer beneath new-tool cycles.

guidance: Which adjacent opportunity reuses capabilities already present?
primary_value: The logical extension is more Lam content per advanced device: gate-all-around surface treatment, atomic-scale conductor etch, high-bandwidth-memory and advanced-packaging processes, plus Equipment Intelligence and Dextro automation across the installed base.

guidance: Which large future outcome still lacks commercial proof?
primary_value: Lam becomes the dominant autonomous-fab productivity layer by combining a massive installed base with Equipment Intelligence and Dextro robotics, creating a materially larger recurring software/service economics stream. Assign no material value until adoption and margins are disclosed.

guidance: Name one measurable development that could beat expectations.
primary_value: AI-driven flash, advanced DRAM, leading-edge foundry and advanced packaging sustain low-$150-billion-plus WFE while Lam's share of WFE approaches the high-30% range and service revenue compounds faster than expected.

guidance: Name one measurable development that could break the thesis.
primary_value: A memory or AI-capex pause combines with tighter China controls and multiple compression, producing a sharp stock decline even if Lam remains a technology leader.

guidance: What should change before the financial result becomes obvious?
primary_value: September-quarter execution is the immediate test: $8.10 billion revenue, 52.0% gross margin, 39.5% operating margin and $2.15 EPS at guidance midpoints, plus commentary on CY2027 WFE, China and CSBG.

guidance: Choose fundamentals, hybrid, catalyst, momentum, narrative, credit, no edge, or insufficient evidence.
primary_value: Fundamental quality-growth story with strong semiconductor-cycle and valuation sensitivity.

guidance: What observable evidence supports this label?
primary_value: Record FY2026 revenue and profits, a greater-than-20% sequential September revenue guide and rising AI-related process complexity are fundamental drivers. The share price also embeds a large duration/multiple component, so expectations matter as much as current results.

guidance: What would meaningfully strengthen or weaken the classification?
primary_value: September-quarter results and 10-Q; updated CY2027 WFE expectations; CSBG growth; China/export-control exposure; Akara, Argos and advanced-packaging adoption; DSO, inventory and free-cash-flow conversion.

guidance: Deep dive, watch for proof, watchlist, trade only, unattractive price, asymmetric trade, pass, or no position.
primary_value: Watchlist; no position. Lam is a high-quality, proven-moat semiconductor-equipment leader, but roughly 50.6x trailing GAAP EPS and 74.6x FY2026 free cash flow at the verified pre-earnings quote leave too little margin of safety. Revisit after a current price refresh, September-quarter proof or a materially lower multiple.

guidance: What missing evidence matters most?
primary_value: The current post-earnings share price; sustainable CY2027 WFE; China-policy impact; normalized service growth; share gains at sub-2nm and next-generation memory nodes; autonomous-fab monetization; customer concentration; and whether working capital normalizes.

guidance: Write the evidence before the next event.
primary_value: Upgrade toward an approved starter position if price-to-normalized earnings falls toward 30-35x while growth, 36-40% operating margins, CSBG momentum and cash conversion remain intact, or if forward earnings rise enough to create the same valuation. Downgrade on guidance failure, share loss or materially tighter export controls.
